extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment & Discipline staff, and other stakeholders in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedures governing disciplinary findings, mitigating factors, remedial measures, sanctions, and notices for patent attorneys/practitioners before the USPTO (OED). Includes jurisdictional basis, misconduct examples (e.g., returned checks), and publication/notice requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction and authority to approve settlements
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary matters and the authority to approve proposed settlement agreements pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. § 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement agreements resolving disciplinary action must be submitted to and may be approved by the Under Secretary/USPTO Director under the cited statutory and regulatory provisions; the Final Order sets forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered practitioner status and applicability of disciplinary rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent who is a patent attorney registered to practice before the Office is subject to the USPTO Disciplinary Rules (37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration number and state bar status are noted; disciplinary rules at 37 C.F.R. govern conduct and enforcement for registered patent practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited conduct — submission of checks returned for insufficient funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting checks to the USPTO that are returned for insufficient funds constitutes a violation (here cited as 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example facts: Respondent signed/submitted five checks totaling $4,665.00 between November 2006 and September 2010 that were returned for insufficient funds. Such conduct, as charged, supports a finding of violation of the cited rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping/accounting obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must keep sufficiently formal accounting records for deposits into and disbursements from business/operating accounts; failure to do so can lead to improper checks and disciplinary action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order notes respondent 'did not always keep sufficiently formal accounting records' which contributed to checks being drawn on insufficient funds. Proper accounting is implied as a professional obligation and a point of evaluation in discipline matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restitution and corrective payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Making good on returned checks and associated fees (restitution) is relevant to the disciplinary evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent made good on all returned checks and returned-check fees after receiving notice; restitution is treated as a mitigating fact in assessing discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial measures (trust account and banking safeguards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementing remedial steps — e.g., opening a new client trust account for government filing fees and authorizing the financial institution to notify the state bar on returned trust checks — is a material mitigating factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific remedial actions cited: (a) opened new client trust account and deposits government filing fees there; (b) authorized bank to notify Florida Bar automatically if a trust account check is returned due to insufficient/uncollected funds, absent bank error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing legal education and training as mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Completing CLE on law firm financial management and client trust account maintenance/management is mitigating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent took two CLE classes (law firm financial management; maintaining/managing client trust account) sponsored by the Florida Bar; such education is credited as remedial and mitigating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Client harm assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the misconduct resulted in harm to clients is a material consideration; absence of harm may mitigate discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this matter it 'does not appear that the submission of the five checks ... resulted in harm to the client's matters,' which the order treats as a mitigating circumstance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traditional mitigating factors considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Length of practice, absence of prior disciplinary history, acceptance of responsibility, and remorse are mitigating factors in determining discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order recites: respondent has been a practitioner for over twenty-five years, has no prior disciplinary history, accepted responsibility unequivocally, and is deeply remorseful; these informed the agreed-upon discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction imposed — public reprimand
rubrics_metrics.description: A public reprimand is an available sanction for specified misconduct and may be imposed as part of a settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agreement/order publicly reprimands the respondent and requires publication of the Final Order and an Official Gazette notice materially consistent with the provided text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and Official Notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order in the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette consistent with the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text of the required Official Gazette notice is provided; publication includes factual summary, identified violation, remedial steps taken, and mitigating factors considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, the OED Director must notify disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where respondent is admitted, courts of admission, and the public of the public discipline and reasons for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order requires the OED Director to transmit notice to relevant state bars and courts; such notice is part of the discipline process and broader accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of record in future proceedings and aggravation/rebuttal
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the settlement prevents the Office from considering the disciplinary record in future complaints or proceedings concerning similar misconduct; prior record may be used as an aggravating factor or to rebut respondent statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order explicitly states the record may be considered (1) when addressing further complaints of same/similar misconduct and/or (2) in future disciplinary proceedings as aggravation or rebuttal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The parties to the settlement bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the agreement unless otherwise provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order states 'The OED Director and Respondent bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.' Cost allocation is therefore a point of negotiation in settlements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement approval produces final order with stipulated facts, conclusions, and sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: A settlement agreement that resolves disciplinary action, when approved by the Director, becomes a Final Order establishing stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order records the parties' stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions and is published; settlements can finalize discipline without contested hearing if approved.
